transcript:
User: Hi — I saw your ad on Facebook about answering missed calls. I keep losing patients after hours, so I'm curious how it works.
Agent: Yeah, that makes sense—after-hours is where a lot of those callers just move on. When someone calls after you’re closed right now, what happens to the call?
User: The call goes to voicemail, and I fear they might end up choosing a competitor instead.
Agent: Right—I hear you; voicemail after hours is where people often just try the next practice. Roughly how many after-hours calls do you think hit voicemail in a typical week?
User: About 20 calls a week go to voicemail, and I think half of those would book if answered.
Agent: Got it—so that’s roughly 10 potential bookings a week slipping away after hours. What’s your average value per new patient visit or case, roughly?
User: The average appointment value is $650.
Agent: Okay—if you booked even 50% of those 20 missed after-hours calls at $650 each, that’s about **$6500 extra a week**… and that’s just one week—about **$28100 over a month**.  

Does that feel pretty accurate based on what you’re seeing?
User: Yes, that sounds accurate. Booking just half would significantly increase our revenue.
Agent: Totally—and that’s exactly what we help you capture when your team can’t get to the phone after hours. It’s a 20-minute walkthrough with Jay so you can see how it works and what the numbers look like for your practice—what’s better for you, later today or tomorrow?
User: I don't need a call with anyone—let's just book the live call slot directly for tomorrow.
Agent: I can do that—before I lock it in, are you looking for **tomorrow morning** or **tomorrow afternoon**?
User: Tomorrow afternoon works best for me.
Agent: Got it—tomorrow afternoon works. What’s your first name?
User: My first name is Maria.
Agent: Thanks, Maria—what’s your last name?
User: It's Gonzales.
Agent: Thanks—what’s the name of your practice?
User: The name of my practice is Bright Smile Dental, located in Chicago.
Agent: Perfect—thanks. And quick check: you’re on **Central time**, right?
User: Yes, that's right. I'm in the Central Time Zone, here in Chicago.
Agent: Great—thanks. And is the number you’re calling from the best contact number to reach you for the SMS confirmation?
User: Yes, my best contact number is +13124001234. Please use this number for SMS confirmation.
User: Mm-hmm.
Agent: Perfect—tomorrow afternoon I can get you in as soon as **1:00 PM** or **1:30 PM** Central time. Which works?
User: Let's book it for 1:30 PM Central time tomorrow, please.
Agent: One sec—I'm locking in tomorrow at 1:30 PM Central for you now.
Agent: Thanks, Maria! You’re all set for **tomorrow at 1:30 PM Central**—you’ll receive an SMS text with the confirmation details so you can add it to your calendar or reschedule if needed.  

Is there anything else I can help you with?
User: Yes, that's perfect — please book it. Thank you for setting up the live call for tomorrow.
Agent: You’re very welcome, Maria—glad we got it set up. Jay’s looking forward to speaking tomorrow at 1:30 PM Central, and you’ll get that SMS confirmation shortly. Have a great rest of your day—bye!
